name: Angel Falls
headline: height
subtitle: Kerepakupai Merú, Canaima National Park, Venezuela
description: Angel Falls, also known as Kerepakupai Merú, is the world's tallest waterfall, in Canaima National Park in Bolívar state, southeastern Venezuela. It pours off the flat-topped Auyán-tepui and falls a total of 979 m (3,212 ft), including a single uninterrupted drop of 807 m (2,648 ft). The falls were named after the American pilot Jimmie Angel, who flew over them in the 1930s.

facts.text: The falls are on a branch of the Carrao River, an upper tributary of the Caroní, and are best seen from the air because of the dense jungle around them.

The height was last surveyed by a National Geographic expedition in 1949. Guinness notes that if only the 807 m drop counted, the 948 m multi-drop Tugela Falls in South Africa would be the tallest waterfall overall.
The Pemón name Kerepakupai Merú means 'waterfall of the deepest place'. In 2009 Venezuela's president declared that this Indigenous name should be used.
Canaima National Park covers about 3 million hectares, and roughly 65% of it is table mountain (tepui) formations.

caveats: No Venezuelan park authority page could be found; UNESCO's Canaima page gives only a rounded 1,000 m for the world's highest waterfall, so the 979 m and 807 m figures come from Britannica and Guinness World Records.
The 979 m total includes cascades below the main plunge; some question whether all of it should count as one waterfall.
Britannica says Jimmie Angel crash-landed nearby in 1937, while Guinness says he recorded the falls after flying over them in November 1933.
The waterfall outline is illustrative; only its height is to scale.
